title: cc-docker project config
description: Schema for .cc-docker/cc-docker.yml — consumed by the cc-config tool (toolchain/config/generate-compose.py) to generate .cc-docker/docker-compose.yml. See the README section 'Configuring cc-docker' for details.

image.description: Legacy mode: prebuilt Docker image to run as the `cc` service, e.g. cc-node20. Mutually exclusive with `modules` — exactly one of the two is required.

modules.description: Modular mode: toolchain stack modules to compose into the image, e.g. [node, zulu]. An empty list [] means base only. Mutually exclusive with `image` — exactly one of the two is required.

git.description: Git identity to configure inside the container.

name.description: Value for git's user.name, exposed to the container as GIT_USER_NAME.

email.description: Value for git's user.email, exposed to the container as GIT_USER_EMAIL.

env.description: Extra environment variables merged into the `cc` service.

readonly.description: If true, all project bind mounts declared in `mounts` are mounted read-only.

display.description: Forward the host's display-server clipboard socket into the container, so `claude` can paste images from the host clipboard. 'auto' detects Wayland vs X11 from the host env vars the `cc` launcher forwards (CC_HOST_WAYLAND_DISPLAY/CC_HOST_DISPLAY) and does nothing if neither is set. 'wayland'/'x11' force a mode. 'disabled' turns off forwarding. (Not 'off': YAML 1.1 parses a bare 'off' as the boolean false.)

mounts.description: Project paths to bind-mount into the container.

path.description: Path to mount, relative to the project root. Use "." to mount the whole project root.

exclude.description: Glob patterns (relative to this mount) to shadow out with a tmpfs (directories) or a read-only /dev/null bind (files).

extra_mounts.description: Raw docker compose volume entries, appended verbatim to the generated `volumes` list. No further validation is applied.

docker_socket.description: Mount the host's /var/run/docker.sock into the container, granting root-equivalent access to the host Docker daemon (it can launch privileged containers with arbitrary host mounts). Disabled by default — only enable this for a project you trust with that level of host access.

anthropic_api_key_file.description: Path on the host to a file whose entire contents are your Anthropic API key. Delivered to the container as a Docker secret mounted at /run/secrets/anthropic_api_key; the entrypoint exports it as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY before launching claude. Never written into the generated compose file or the container environment. Supports a leading ~ (host home) and absolute paths. Optional — omit to keep using the mounted ~/.claude OAuth login.
